@dev Implementation of the {IERC20} interface.
 This implementation is agnostic to the way tokens are created. This means
 that a supply mechanism has to be added in a derived contract using {_mint}.
 TIP: For a detailed writeup see our guide
 https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/how-to-implement-erc20-supply-mechanisms/226[How
 to implement supply mechanisms].
 The default value of {decimals} is 18. To change this, you should override
 this function so it returns a different value.
 We have followed general OpenZeppelin Contracts guidelines: functions revert
 instead returning `false` on failure. This behavior is nonetheless
 conventional and does not conflict with the expectations of ERC-20
 applications.

@dev Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation.

 no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including

@dev Variant of {invMod}. More efficient, but only works if `p` is known to be a prime greater than `2`.

 prime, then `a**(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p`. As a consequence, we have `a * a**(p-2) ≡ 1 mod p`, which means that
 `a**(p-2)` is the modular multiplicative inverse of a in Fp.

@title SavingsVault (Lockbox)
 @notice Lock a single, pre-configured stablecoin until a chosen maturity date.
 Trust model — there is deliberately no owner, admin, pause, upgrade or
 emergency path. Every parameter is fixed at deployment:
   - `token`, `treasury`, `feeBps` and `minLockDuration` are immutable.
   - A vault's `maturity` is written once at creation and never modified.
   - Only the vault owner can withdraw, only once, only at/after maturity.
   - Fees are accrued, not pushed. `withdraw` only transfers to the vault
     owner, so a problem with the treasury (e.g. the token issuer blocking
     it) can never block anyone's principal. Anyone may call `claimFees`
     to send accrued fees — and only accrued fees — to the fixed treasury.
 Fee policy — `feeBps` (25 = 0.25%) of the principal is deducted at
 withdrawal and accrued for `treasury`. Rounded down, so the user is never
 charged more than the stated rate. Because `feeBps` is immutable, the fee a
 user sees when depositing is the fee they will pay when withdrawing.
 Decimals — all accounting is in the token's raw base units; the contract
 never scales amounts, so it is correct for 6- or 18-decimal tokens alike.
 `decimals()` is checked at deployment against what the deployer expects
 to catch pointing the vault at the wrong token.
 Unsupported tokens — deposits verify the exact amount arrived, so
 fee-on-transfer tokens are rejected. Rebasing tokens are NOT supported
 (a negative rebase could make later withdrawals fail); deploy only
 against plain ERC-20 stablecoins such as USD₮.
@notice Hard cap so a typo at deployment can't create an abusive fee.
@notice Hard cap so a typo in the UI can't lock funds for centuries.
@notice Fees earned from completed withdrawals, not yet sent to `treasury`.

@notice Lock `amount` (token base units) for `lockDuration` seconds.
 @dev Caller must first `approve` this contract for `amount`.

SafeCast.metadata: {"compiler":{"version":"0.8.28+commit.7893614a"},"language":"Solidity","output":{"abi":[{"inputs":[{"internalType":"uint8","name":"bits","type":"uint8"},{"internalType":"int256","name":"value","type":"int256"}],"name":"SafeCastOverflowedIntDowncast","type":"error"},{"inputs":[{"internalType":"int256","name":"value","type":"int256"}],"name":"SafeCastOverflowedIntToUint","type":"error"},{"inputs":[{"internalType":"uint8","name":"bits","type":"uint8"},{"internalType":"uint256","name":"value","type":"uint256"}],"name":"SafeCastOverflowedUintDowncast","type":"error"},{"inputs":[{"internalType":"uint256","name":"value","type":"uint256"}],"name":"SafeCastOverflowedUintToInt","type":"error"}],"devdoc":{"details":"Wrappers over Solidity's uintXX/intXX/bool casting operators with added overflow checks. Downcasting from uint256/int256 in Solidity does not revert on overflow. This can easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows. Trust model \u2014 there is deliberately no owner, admin, pause, upgrade or emergency path. Every parameter is fixed at deployment:   - `token`, `treasury`, `feeBps` and `minLockDuration` are immutable.   - A vault's `maturity` is written once at creation and never modified.   - Only the vault owner can withdraw, only once, only at/after maturity.   - Fees are accrued, not pushed. `withdraw` only transfers to the vault     owner, so a problem with the treasury (e.g. the token issuer blocking     it) can never block anyone's principal. Anyone may call `claimFees`     to send accrued fees \u2014 and only accrued fees \u2014 to the fixed treasury. Fee policy \u2014 `feeBps` (25 = 0.25%) of the principal is deducted at withdrawal and accrued for `treasury`. Rounded down, so the user is never charged more than the stated rate. Because `feeBps` is immutable, the fee a user sees when depositing is the fee they will pay when withdrawing. Decimals \u2014 all accounting is in the token's raw base units; the contract never scales amounts, so it is correct for 6- or 18-decimal tokens alike. `decimals()` is checked at deployment against what the deployer expects to catch pointing the vault at the wrong token.
